raw_response:
I’ve been farming these 20.8 mu for 30 years, since I was 22. I never went to school, but I know this land better than anyone. My family has three people — my husband works construction in the county town and comes home on weekends, so mostly it’s me on the farm. My daughter is married and lives nearby, but she has her own family to feed. I do the day-to-day work, and my husband helps at planting and harvest.

**Winter wheat**

I’ll plant wheat in the first week of October, same as always. If you plant too late, the wheat won’t survive the winter well. I buy common wheat seed from Old Zhang’s shop in the village — about 15 kg per mu, costs around 20 yuan. I used to save my own seed, but the yield got worse year after year, so now I buy fresh every two or three years.

Before planting, I hire a tractor to rotary-till the field. Then I spread fertilizer — about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, that’s most of a standard bag. I know Wang sister-in-law down the road puts a whole bag, but her son has a factory job and they have more money. My family is not poor, but we can’t throw money at the field. I also need to keep some cash for my husband’s medicine and for the New Year.

In March when the wheat turns green, I go look at it. If it looks yellow and weak, I spread about 10 kg of urea per mu as topdressing. If it looks green enough, maybe I use less. Last year I used about 10 kg and it was fine. I irrigate twice — once before winter to protect the seedlings, and once at jointing in April. Pumping water costs electricity money, about 25 yuan each time per mu. Some people water three or four times, but I think twice is enough if the spring rain comes. I spray herbicide once in early spring.

I expect about 400 kg per mu if the weather is normal. Last year I got 380, the year before 420.

**Summer maize**

The wheat harvest is in early June, and I have to plant corn within a few days — the window is very tight. I hire a combine for wheat harvest, then quickly do light rotary tillage and plant the maize. I use hybrid corn seed, about 45 yuan per mu. I put about 35 kg of compound fertilizer in the planting hole. Some people topdress corn too, but I usually don’t — the base fertilizer is enough, and corn is tougher than wheat.

For corn, I irrigate once at the big trumpet stage in August if it hasn’t rained. If the rain is good, maybe I don’t water at all. Corn doesn’t need as much fuss as wheat. I spray herbicide once after planting. I hope for 450 kg per mu. Last year I got 460, which was a good year.

**Labor and money**

I do most of the spreading, irrigating, and spraying myself. My husband helps at the busy times. I hire people for wheat harvest and for a few days when we’re rushing to plant corn after the wheat comes off. Hired labor is 100 yuan per day now, which is expensive, so I keep it to the minimum. The seed, fertilizer, water, pesticide, and hired help will cost about 10,000 yuan for the year. That’s a lot, but we have some income from my husband’s work. I just hope the weather is good and prices don’t drop.
